subject: Trial success criteria & POC plan — Redwood / AstraHealth
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@astrahealth.com>, AstraHealth Procurement <procurement@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: proposed trial KPIs, ownership, next steps

Hi Rajiv — great speaking with you today. Thanks again for the time and the clear description of the clinical routing workload. Per our discussion, I put together a concise set of proposed success criteria and a pragmatic timeline to validate viability in a 4–6 week trial. Please review and flag anything you want tweaked.

Quick recap / objectives:
- Validate model-driven clinical routing at production latency and cost targets.
- Measure quality against your labeled set (triage accuracy + hallucination rate).
- Surface operational metrics (p95 latency, sustained throughput, per-token cost).

Proposed trial success criteria (measurable):
1) Latency: p95 inference latency < 200 ms (API end-to-end, sample 1k requests).
2) Throughput: sustained 150–200 reqs/sec with 99% success rate for 30-minute windows.
3) Cost: target average token cost <= $0.0009/token for the evaluated model/config.
4) Quality: accuracy on your labeled dev set >= 89% (precision on triage class labels) and hallucination rate < 1% on a held-out subset.
5) Reliability: error rate < 0.5% and full end-to-end logs for audit samples.

Ownership and points of contact:
- Redwood sales / trial lead: Monica Patel (me) — trial coordination, choreography with your team.
- Redwood pricing & provisioning: Ben Carter — dedicated pool sizing and cost estimate.
- Redwood CS / evaluation support: Neha Kapoor — setup, evaluation harness, and runbooks.
- AstraHealth: Rajiv Shah (technical sponsor), Procurement contact included for contracting/PO.

High-level timeline (suggested):
- Week 0 (kickoff): agree on dataset access, SLAs, and MOP.
- Week 1: environment setup and sample ingest (sanitized subset).
- Week 2: small-scale smoke tests and latency/throughput tuning.
- Week 3: run full evaluation on labeled dev set and measure quality metrics.
- Week 4: address tuning items, iterate; run second pass if needed.
- Week 5–6: final readout and decision.

Attachments: I attached a short MOP draft (astra_poc_mop_v1.pdf) and a sample prompts file (sample_prompts.csv) you can use to sanity-check the evaluation harness.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Rajiv: confirm the proposed KPIs above or suggest adjustments by EOD Thu.
- Procurement: can you share any PO or contracting constraints we should plan for?
- Redwood (Ben/Neha): can you prepare an initial cost estimate and an Ops checklist ahead of kickoff?

If that sounds good I can lock a kickoff for the week of Aug 4th.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel | Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@astrahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: AstraHealth Procurement <procurement@astrahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: proposed trial KPIs, ownership, next steps

Monica — thanks for the crisp recap and the list. A few clarifications from our side: we like the latency and throughput targets, but need to confirm two items before we commit to the timeline: (1) SOC 2 / security evidence for the hosted trial (we require this for any externally hosted inference), and (2) an estimate of token consumption and expected monthly spend for an initial 4-week run using ~10M tokens.

On quality: our labeled dev set is ~7k examples; can you confirm your evaluation harness can run against that dataset and provide per-intent precision/recall? Also, how will Redwood measure hallucination rate — are you able to provide a simple tooling approach (we can provide labels where available)?

Procurement side: we have standard terms and need to understand typical lead time for an SOW/PO versus a simple pilot agreement. If you can loop in pricing and procurement, that will help accelerate.

I’ve copied procurement; they prefer a 30–45 day review window for any SOW. If the SOC 2 evidence is available and we get a rough cost estimate by Friday, we can still hit an Aug 4 kickoff.

Thanks — Rajiv
Rajiv Shah | Dir. ML Ops, AstraHealth
rajiv@astrahealth.com

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Jul 2025 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: proposed trial KPIs, ownership, next steps

Rajiv — appreciated, and thanks for the quick note. Answers inline below and next steps at the bottom.

SOC 2 / security: we can provide standard SOC 2 Type II evidence along with a shorter security snapshot (network/crypto controls) for your review. I will attach the SOC 2 binder link in the follow-up and Ben can confirm any additional onboarding checks.

Token estimate and cost: Ben, can you provide a rough estimate here (I asked to be looped in)? As a ballpark, for the model we demoed, a 10M-token run is typically in the $6k–$10k range depending on batching / quantization. I’ll get a more precise number from Ben by EOD Friday.

Evaluation harness: yes — Neha will run the labeled set through our eval harness and deliver per-intent precision/recall, false-positive rates, and a small hallucination check (manual adjudication on a 200-sample subset). If you can provide the labeled dev set in a sanitized CSV (or a secure S3 share), we’ll ingest and run the first pass.

Proposed kickoff: Aug 4 (week of) — below are concrete owners and milestones:
- Aug 4 (Kickoff): exchange sanitized dataset + onboarding credentials; agree MOP final.
- Aug 5–8: ingestion and smoke tests (Neha + Astra infra).
- Aug 11–15: tuning window — run evaluation harness + initial readout.
- Aug 18–22: iterate on tuning; second pass if needed.
- Aug 25–29: final readout and decision.

Ben / Neha — action items:
- Ben: draft a one-page cost estimate for a 4-week trial (include dedicated pool vs hosted API delta), and confirm if we can support the requested latency targets with the proposed config.
- Neha: prepare the eval harness checklist and a short script we can run on the 7k-example dev set.

Rajiv / Procurement — action items:
- Please share the labeled dev set via secure share and any legal constraints (PII, redaction rules) so we can plan data handling.
- Procurement: confirm expected review window for a pilot agreement (Rajiv mentioned 30–45 days).

I’ll attach the MOP and sample prompts now (see attachments). If procurement needs a pilot SOW template we can provide a lightweight one.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel | Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 31 Jul 2025 01:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: initial cost sketch for AstraHealth trial

Internal note — keeping Rajiv/procurement off this thread for now.

Short estimate based on the configuration we demoed:
- Model + dedicated development GPU pool for trial (single-node multi-GPU pool): est $8,200/month for a reserved pilot pool.
- 10M tokens guidance: ~ $7,500 total with typical batching/kv-cache savings (we assume 12-token average response; numbers vary with prompt length).
- Per-token target: we can hit ~$0.00075–0.0009/token depending on batching and quantization.

Latency feasibility: we should be able to meet p95 < 200ms for the sample sizes discussed with the right batch config and a small dedicated pool. I’ll confirm after we validate sequence length distribution from their sample set.

Next actions (internal):
- Neha: prep the eval harness and a quick runbook for dataset ingestion.
- Monica: once Rajiv shares dataset and SOC2 acceptance criteria, we can finalize the SOW template and send a light pilot agreement.

Ben
Ben Carter | Head of Pricing & Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
